sources.title: MySQL 8.4 point-in-time recovery using binary log
MySQL 8.4 point-in-time recovery using event positions

claims.text: MySQL 8.4 documents that physical backups are raw directory/file copies and are suitable for large important databases needing fast recovery; logical backups store database structure and content representations and are suitable for smaller data, editable values or structures, and recreation on different machine architectures.

MySQL 8.4 defines point-in-time recovery as typically restoring a full backup to the state at backup time and then bringing the server forward incrementally from the full-backup time to a more recent time.

MySQL 8.4 documents that PITR information comes from binary logs generated after the full backup; binary logging must be enabled, MySQL 8.4 enables it by default, SHOW BINARY LOGS lists log files, SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS reports the current log, and mysqlbinlog can select log sections by event time or position. Applying its output reexecutes represented data modifications.

MySQL 8.4's event-position recovery example says to restore the last full backup before the desired point, use the last restored binary-log position supplied by the backup/restore tool rather than infer it from InnoDB display output, find the precise event position before the point of interest by inspecting mysqlbinlog output, and apply from the restored start position to the stop position before the unwanted event. It explicitly recommends using datetime options only to locate actual event positions, then using start/stop position to apply the range because datetime range application has higher risk of missing events.

findings: 备份方式、PITR 的 position 起止边界、连续日志链、隔离验证和演练已覆盖。
备份一致性坐标与备份基线的对应、以及并发写入、DDL、非事务表边界缺少一手证据；机制题专项维度低于最低分。
